The MonsGeek FUN60 Ultra TMR is my pick for the best TMR keyboard under $100, assuming you're buying primarily for competitive gaming and are happy with a compact 60% layout. RTINGS' testing found its performance close to much more expensive gaming keyboards, and it has an aluminum case, Rapid Trigger, adjustable actuation, and 8,000Hz polling.

75% wireless keyboard with a function row and Rapid Trigger. Worth considering if you need more keys, though I have less independent performance-test evidence for it.

What I'd buy: the FUN60 Ultra TMR wireless at $90 or less. Its combination of independently tested gaming performance, build quality, and switch flexibility is unusually strong for the price. The main caveats are short battery life at 8K wireless and the inconvenient connection-mode switch beneath Caps Lock.

chats.answer:
I'd buy the EPOMAKER HE65 V2 TMR. EPOMAKER currently lists it for $59.99, and it has nearly everything I'd look for in a sub-$100 magnetic gaming keyboard without sacrificing arrow keys. 
EPOMAKER

EPOMAKER HE65 V2 TMR

$59.99 direct

EPOMAKER

65% layout with arrows; Rapid Trigger and adjustable actuation; advertised 8,000 Hz wired and 2.4 GHz wireless; Bluetooth; supports magnetic and standard mechanical switches.

The main alternative is the MonsGeek FUN60 Ultra TMR, typically $80–90. I'd choose it instead if you specifically want a CNC aluminum case and a smaller 60% layout for FPS gaming. It also offers Rapid Trigger and 8K polling, but lacks dedicated arrows, and some owners have reported firmware or detection issues. Make sure you select the TMR variant. 
MKB Guide
+1

One caveat: I'm assuming US pricing before tax and prioritizing gaming. I haven't independently measured either board's latency, so I wouldn't treat the advertised 8K polling or tiny actuation increments as proof that one is faster. At the current $59.99 price, the EPOMAKER is my better all-around buy.
